runs.text: <<h|ɑ|ˈ|m|ɑ|s>> and Palestinians are not the same. Here it is, in nine words. At work, you condemn <<h|ɑ|ˈ|m|ɑ|s>>. A colleague asks: so you hate Palestinians? <<h|ɑ|ˈ|m|ɑ|s>> is a terror group. Palestinians are a people. Gaza hasn't had an election since two thousand and six, and about half of its people are children. None of them ever voted for <<h|ɑ|ˈ|m|ɑ|s>>. And in March twenty twenty five, Gazans marched in the streets, chanting: <<h|ɑ|ˈ|m|ɑ|s>> out. Save this. Against <<h|ɑ|ˈ|m|ɑ|s>>. Not against Palestinians. Which sentence do you need most? Tell me in the comments. A terror group, or a people? nine words tell them apart.
